BLOCKING (PR defect, Windows leg): scripts/package-component.sh:152-156 replaced the portable '(cd dir && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS)' with a manual 'read -r digest name' loop. Git-Bash/MSYS sha256sum writes '<hex> *<target>.tar.gz', so name keeps the '*' and the loop resolves 'dist/*x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.tar.gz'. CI jobs 119940944821 / 119940996398, step 'Build and pack the target tarball': sha256sum: '.../dist/*x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.tar.gz': No such file or directory. Reproduced locally with an MSYS-format manifest: old sha256sum -c => OK, new loop => identical error.
Second Windows defect behind it: scripts/make-component-dist.sh:395,410 writes the MSYS '*' marker into the sidecar and SHA256SUMS, which scripts/component_release.py:461,508 rejects, so the Windows catalog step fails even if only the shell loop is patched. Fix the writer (force GNU text format or generate manifests in Python) and add a '*' fixture to scripts/tests/component-release.test.sh.

1) package-component.sh reads SHA256SUMS itself: strips the optional Git-Bash/MSYS '*' marker, requires a 64-hex digest, rejects any name containing '/', and re-hashes every entry in default (binary) mode instead of check mode. Simulated MSYS writer output ('<hex> *<name>') is accepted; deleting the strip line or injecting './name' fails; CRLF and wrong-digest manifests fail closed.
2) make-component-dist.sh emits sidecar and SHA256SUMS through sha256_line, always canonical '<hex>  <name>'; the digest still comes from the default binary computation. Post-write verification re-hashes each file instead of 'sha256sum -c'.
3) component_release.py cargo_version treats version.workspace = true as inherited and resolves [workspace.package].version; explicit versions remain strict X.Y.Z. The test script uses portable sha256()/sed_inplace(); no GNU-only sha256sum or sed -i remains in component-release.test.sh.
